title: Relay each terminal's PIN so the host can read it

blocks.text: A shop's PIN pads send their purchases through `PinRelay` to the acquirer's host. The host reads PIN blocks in one way only: ISO format 0 under the PIN key it shares with the relay (`hostPinKey`). The terminals are less tidy. Each has its own PIN key, and the shop runs two models: the older one sends ISO format 0, the newer one ISO format 1. The relay's `terminals` map knows each terminal's key and format.

items: cardholders who swipe their card and type a PIN are always declined. A swiped purchase can arrive with no field 2, only the card's track 2 in field 35;
on the new model, every PIN purchase is declined;
last month a PIN pad's key fell out of step after a repair, and for an afternoon the host approved its purchases without checking any PIN.

blocks.text: Finish the two methods marked `TODO` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PinRelay.java`: `cardNumber` and `putHostPin`. `send` and `refusal` already work; when `putHostPin` returns `false`, `send` answers the terminal itself. About fifteen lines in total.

The tests run a real `JCESecurityModule` on both sides, with test keys and the test cards `4111111111111111` and `5555555555554444`. The host behind the fake `MUX` reads each PIN block it receives and declines with `55` when it can't find the cardholder's PIN.

cases.says: a chip purchase from a terminal reaches the host with a PIN block the host reads as the PIN the cardholder typed
the host receives the terminal's fields unchanged and an 8-byte block that is not the terminal's, and a purchase without a PIN passes as it is
a format 0 block is tied to the card number, so for a swiped card without field 2 the card number comes from track 2
translation changes the format as well as the key: a terminal's ISO format 1 block reaches the host in the format the host reads
a block the module cannot translate stops the purchase at the relay; it never reaches the host without its PIN

origin.section: 7.3 The Client Translates the PIN and Never Sees It

concepts: A format 0 PIN block is the PIN mixed with 12 digits of the card number and encrypted under a PIN key, so reading it takes both the key and the card number.
The client re-encrypts a PIN block from the terminal's key and format to the host's with translatePIN, and refuses a purchase whose block cannot be translated rather than sending it without field 52.
